# Disproof: The Statement is FALSE

## Counterexample

Consider the path graph on 4 vertices with $a = \tfrac{3}{5}$. Define:

$$G = \frac{3}{5}\begin{pmatrix} 0 & 1 & 0 & 0 \\ 1 & 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 0 \end{pmatrix}, \qquad A = I + G = \begin{pmatrix} 1 & \tfrac{3}{5} & 0 & 0 \\ \tfrac{3}{5} & 1 & \tfrac{3}{5} & 0 \\ 0 & \tfrac{3}{5} & 1 & \tfrac{3}{5} \\ 0 & 0 & \tfrac{3}{5} & 1 \end{pmatrix}$$

### Verification of all hypotheses

**$G_{ii}=0$, $G_{ij}\in\{0,a\}$, $a\in[0,1)$, $G$ symmetric:** Immediate from construction ($a=\tfrac{3}{5}<1$).

**$A$ is positive definite:** Compute the leading principal minors $D_k$ via the tridiagonal recurrence $D_k = D_{k-1} - a^2 D_{k-2}$:

$$D_1 = 1, \quad D_2 = 1 - \tfrac{9}{25} = \tfrac{16}{25}, \quad D_3 = \tfrac{16}{25} - \tfrac{9}{25}\cdot 1 = \tfrac{7}{25}, \quad D_4 = \tfrac{7}{25} - \tfrac{9}{25}\cdot\tfrac{16}{25} = \tfrac{175-144}{625} = \tfrac{31}{625}.$$

All $D_k > 0$, so $A$ is positive definite. ✓

**$B = A^{-1}$ is SPD with $B_{ii} > 1$:** Since $A$ is SPD, $B$ is automatically SPD. We compute $B_{ii}$ via cofactors. Since $\det(A) = \tfrac{31}{625}$:

- $C_{11} = \det\begin{pmatrix}1&\tfrac35&0\\\tfrac35&1&\tfrac35\\0&\tfrac35&1\end{pmatrix} = \tfrac{7}{25}$, so $B_{11} = \frac{7/25}{31/625} = \frac{175}{31} \approx 5.65 > 1$. ✓

- $C_{22} = \det\begin{pmatrix}1&0&0\\0&1&\tfrac35\\0&\tfrac35&1\end{pmatrix} = \tfrac{16}{25}$, so $B_{22} = \frac{16/25}{31/625} = \frac{400}{31} \approx 12.9 > 1$. ✓

By symmetry of the path graph: $B_{33} = B_{22} = \tfrac{400}{31} > 1$ ✓ and $B_{44} = B_{11} = \tfrac{175}{31} > 1$ ✓.

### The violation: $B_{13} > B_{11}$

Compute the cofactor $C_{13}$ (remove row 1, column 3):

$$M_{13} = \begin{pmatrix} \tfrac35 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & \tfrac35 & \tfrac35 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 \end{pmatrix}, \qquad \det(M_{13}) = \tfrac35\cdot\tfrac35 = \tfrac{9}{25}.$$

Since $(-1)^{1+3}=1$, $C_{13} = \tfrac{9}{25}$, and

$$B_{13} = \frac{C_{13}}{\det(A)} = \frac{9/25}{31/625} = \frac{225}{31} \approx 7.26.$$

Now compare:

$$B_{13} = \frac{225}{31} \;>\; B_{11} = \frac{175}{31}, \qquad \text{since } 225 > 175.$$

This violates $B_{ii} > B_{ij}$ for $i=1,\, j=3$.

### Conclusion

All hypotheses of the problem are satisfied, yet $B_{13} > B_{11}$, contradicting the claim $B_{ii} > B_{ij}$ for all $i \neq j$. The statement is **FALSE**.
